newsitem.title: UK: UK travel agent hits "premature" '98 summer launch.
newsitem.headline: UK travel agent hits "premature" '98 summer launch.

text.p: Travel agent Thomas Cook on Thursday attacked major tour operators for launching 1998 summer holiday brochures before most Britons have jetted off in search of the sun this year.
Thomson, the largest tour operator in the UK with a 30 percent share of the market, is putting its 1998 summer packages on sale from Friday.
Airtours Plc, which took more than three million people away last year, will launch its new brochures on Saturday.
But Thomas Cook, majority owned by Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale, said the move would confuse customers and put pressure on travel agency staff.

"There's early and there's downright premature, and I think tour operators are really pushing their luck launching 1998's summer holidays before anyone's even been away this year," Dido Harding, Thomas Cook's retail marketing director said in a statement.
"Most people are still looking forward to and saving up for this year's break," she added. "Do tour operators really expect people to think that far ahead?"

Airtours said its launch -- two months earlier than last year -- coincided with the return of the "feelgood" factor to the UK economy and came at a time when millions of Britons were enjoying windfall gains from building society flotations.
It quoted research as saying more than 85 percent of holidaymakers want to receive next year's brochure within a month of returning from vacation.
A Thomson spokeswoman said that "there was strong pent-up demand for holidays this year and next".
Thomson and Airtours also run their own high street travel agency operations, part of an industry that sells some 10 million overseas holidays every summer.
The combined effects of the strong pound and early booking discounts mean that 1998 packages are being sold at substantial discounts to trips to the same locations this summer.
